hints: Focus on what causes the colour, only brown $\text{NO}_2$ shows colour while $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ is colourless.
Count the gas moles, 2 moles on the left versus 1 mole on the right, so increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles.
Look at $\Delta H = -57$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ to see the forward reaction is exothermic, so think which direction heating will favour to make more brown gas.
walkthrough:
**Link colour to equilibrium position**

Only $\text{NO}_2$ is brown, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ is colourless. More $\text{NO}_2$ means darker brown, more $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ means lighter.

$$2\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$$
$$\text{brown} \qquad \text{colourless}$$

**Apply Le Chatelier for pressure**

Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas to reduce pressure. Left has 2 moles, right has 1 mole, so equilibrium shifts right toward $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.

$$\text{shift right: less brown } \text{NO}_2, \text{ more colourless } \text{N}_2\text{O}_4$$

**Apply Le Chatelier for temperature**

Forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H$ negative). Increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat, which is the reverse reaction.

$$\text{shift left: more brown } \text{NO}_2$$

**Deduce the colour changes**

Higher pressure gives less $\text{NO}_2$, so colour becomes lighter. Higher temperature gives more $\text{NO}_2$, so colour becomes darker.

options.A: Incorrect. Increasing temperature does give darker colour, but increasing pressure shifts to $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ with fewer moles, so colour lightens, not darkens.
options.B: Incorrect. This row is the reverse of the truth. It confuses the mole count and the sign of $\Delta H$, predicting more $\text{NO}_2$ at high pressure and less $\text{NO}_2$ at high temperature.
options.C: Correct. High pressure favours 1 mole of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ over 2 moles of $\text{NO}_2$, so brown colour fades lighter. High temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction, making more brown $\text{NO}_2$, so colour darkens.
options.D: Incorrect. Increasing pressure does give lighter colour, but increasing temperature favours the reverse endothermic change to make more brown $\text{NO}_2$, so colour darkens, not lightens.
